Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second essay as the umpires make their way out to the middle. Slight delay as there is a little issue at the bowling crease, getting fixed at the moment as groundstaff is hammering ground near bowling crease. Mohammad Naim and Mehidy Hasan are the two openers for Bangladesh. Kasun Rajitha to start the attack for Sri Lanka. Bangladesh to chase 258. Let's play!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Sri Lanka struggled to keep the momentum throughout the inning and wickets at regular intervals did not help their cause. Sadeera Samarawickrama's inning helped them set a target that their bowlers can bowl at but they will require to pull off a special effort. They have the bowling unit to put pressure on a batting side that has struggled a couple of times in this tournament. Bangladesh will need a good start from their openers to help set a platform to pull off a successful run chase. Will they be able to exact revenge for their loss in the group stages? Or will Sri Lanka be able to achieve their second-longest winning streak in this format? We will find out shortly when we return for Bangladesh’s reply.

Sadeera Samarawickrama is up for a chat. He says that the wicket was not easy to bat at the start and they were facing a little difficulty in picking up singles. He adds that he planned to play the ball late under his eyes and that is what got him the results. He mentions that the wicket is not easy to bat against the spinners as the ball is holding onto the surface. He ends by saying that 257 is a good score on this wicket under these conditions.

The Sri Lankan openers got off to a brisk start but the islanders lost Dimuth Karunaratne early in the Powerplay. Kusal Mendis joined forces with Pathum Nissanka and looked to build the innings as they accumulated 74 runs in 107 deliveries for the second wicket. Both the batters departed in quick succession with Pathum Nissanka falling 10 runs short of his half-century and Mendis being dismissed right after he reached his fifty. Sadeera Samarawickrama held up one end thereafter but Charith Asalanka and Dhananjaya de Silva could not build a decent partnership as they fell cheaply. Dasun Shanaka played the supporting role as Sadeera reached his half-century and began going after the bowlers in the death overs. The two of them added 60 runs together but the skipper departed looking to be innovative with his shot-play. Sadeera was dismissed on the last ball of the inning on 93 in deliveries as he helped his side beyond the 250-run mark and it will be interesting to see if the Lankan bowlers can make a game out of this.

A good inning by Sadeera Samarawickrama has helped his side reach of fighting total! Bangladesh will be relatively happy with their bowling performance. They have managed to restrict the hosts to a reasonable target of 257 runs and will feel like they have the batting prowess to chase down this target but would have liked to concede 10-15 runs less in the death overs. Taskin Ahmed and Shoriful Islam were unable to make an impact with the new ball and the introduction of Hasan Mahmud helped them draw first blood. They were unable to take a wicket for a considerable period of time and the reintroduction of Shoriful resulted in the dismissal of both the set batters. Taskin and Mahmud took a wicket a piece to send half their opponent's side back to the shed and the Bangla Tigers looked well in control of the game. They seemed to be losing their discipline towards the end but Mahmud returned to get a crucial wicket and a run out. Taskin Ahmed did manage to take a couple of wickets in the last over but conceded 11 runs.

OUT! Caught at deep midwicket! Taskin Ahmed having the last laugh by bowling a slower ball at the stumps from back of length to which Sadeera Samarawickrama plays the pull shot but couldnt find the timing he was looking for, ends up finding Mahedi Hasan at deep mid wicket boundary. Sri Lanka finish 257/9 after 50 overs.

They will want to build a good partnership here but first up they will have to negotiate with Taskin Ahmed who has the new ball in his hands. Let's play...

We are moments away from the start of the game but first, the two sets of players and the match officials line up for the national anthems. It will be the national anthem of Bangladesh first followed by Sri Lanka's national anthem.

Dasun Shanaka, the captain of Sri Lanka and also the birthday boy says that he is happy with the decision as he would have liked to bat first since the wicket looks used. Adds that there will be good help to the new ball under the lights in the second innings. He speaks about the previous game going down to the wire and adds that they have been a confident side which helped them gain much resistance in the last game. Informs that there are no changes on the side. Mentions that the team talks have been about process and the roles have been straightforward for the batters to score crucial runs while the bowlers look to pick up the wickets.

Shakib Al Hasan, the skipper of Bangladesh says that they will look to bowl as there can be some rain around and they playing an extra bowler so they want to restrict Sri Lanka to as low a score as possible. He talks about the travelling and adapting the conditions as they have been playing both in Sri Lanka and Pakistan. He adds that it is a must win game for their side and the boys are really ready as they look forward to the game.

The side is lacking runs from the top order which is making it difficult for the finishers to play their natural game and they would be hoping that the top-order batters put up a performance like they did when they played Afghanistan. Bowling looks solid for the Bangla Tigers and they did trouble Lankan batters earlier in the Asia Cup campaign. Can the Islanders continue to add to that winning streak or will the giant killers bounce back from the last game? We will find out soon. Stay tuned as we bring you the toss and team updates.

It was a lucky escape for the islanders in their last group stage game because if the Afghans had got their math right with the scenarios for a superior net run rate, they would have been here instead of the hosts. They have had their trouble with the batting lineup and are still searching for a solid start from their top-order batters. One positive for the side has been the emergence of key contributions at crucial junctions of the game. The side needs to improve their batting if they are to challenge for the Aisa Cup title.

We are back after a small break of 2 days in the Asia Cup and what a contest we have on our hands with the Lions from Sri Lanka taking on the Tigers from Bangladesh at the R.Premadasa Stadium, Colombo for the second game of Super Four. Sri Lanka is on a serious winning streak of 12 games in ODI cricket and would be looking to extend that against Bangladesh. The side is missing out on big names from their squad for the Asia Cup but is going along well with a collective team effort on multiple occasions. In their last game of the group stage the Lanks Lions just managed to jump the Afghan hurdle in a close affair that helped them seal the top spot in the group after staring at an early exit from the competition had Afghan managed to get the calculation right and act accordingly. Charith Asalanka and Kusal Mendis have been amongst run-getters for the Islanders but the side would be wanting a lot more from their batters if they are to travel the distance in this Asia Cup campaign. The bowling has been the one that has aided them on multiple occasions with the youngster Matheesha Pathirana taking up the responsibility in the absence of Wanidu to give his side breakthroughs at key moments of the game. Matheesha Pathirana is well helped by his teammates Maheesh Theekshana and Dunith Wellalage. The side needs to figure out their batting against a pumped-up bowling attack of their opponents. Bangladesh is coming into this game already behind the others with a hefty negative NRR after a thumping from Pakistan in the last game. The side has had a hot and cold kind of run in this campaign as they have been bowled out twice under 200 while in the other game against the Afghans they scored in excess of 330. Najmul Shanto has been amongst runs being the top run-getters for them in this campaign's Asia Cup but his removal from the squad after an injury was a massive setback for Bangladesh and his absence was really felt by them in the last game.
